reason: The loop-control rewrite is a small, measurable compiler experiment, but no evidence shows loop control is a bottleneck or that it will help. Combining the Strassen allocations is also a small change, though it retains the measured wrapper’s dominant work; explicit NEON packing may duplicate compiler vectorization. Removing Strassen’s output zero pass is a distinct, low-cost variant, but the measured three-buffer wrapper lost all ten pairs. The 32-row classical path has more upside potential, with meaningful correctness and code-generation risk. The proposed Strassen product-buffer layout appears to match the already measured three-buffer schedule, so verify that it is distinct before implementation. Fused transpose repeats A loads many times and has high implementation risk. Tail splitting does not affect the timed n=512 path.
